results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 68 aligned summaries state the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in spec order (scene: meeting with the third finding, bill, causes, ring, question; concepts; doors, provenance, stages, gate lesson, documents, timing, Barcelona; privacy; derivatives; lifecycle; hashing incl. the Lyon split; understanding; rich media; in practice; trade-offs; verticals; failure modes; CA view; questions; conclusion). The five callouts match no spec paragraph and are recorded as null.

Only scene ¶1 was marked two_ideas (Julien's two documents / Tradeyard GPS finding on Femke's photos). Spec p05 declares both ideas in its controlling idea, so the paragraph holds the one idea its spec entry gives it.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: scene to S4/S5, concepts and understanding/rich media to S1, pipeline (incl. provenance and documents) to S2/S3, privacy to S3, derivatives and lifecycle to S4 (lifecycle also S3), hashing to S5, in-practice to S1/S3/S4/S5, the judgement sections and conclusion to the whole thesis.

Each evidence item is followed by its meaning: Figures 1-6 carry interpretive captions; the nine-stage table is framed by its lead-in and read in 'What blocks publication'; the retention table by the deletion and hash-retention paragraphs; the cost table by the processing-line paragraph; the trade-offs and vertical tables by their lead-ins and follow-ups; quotations (Rightmove, OLX Dali, YAMS, ClamAV, PDQ, Autotrader, mobile.de) each get a sentence saying what they show.

All other boundaries express their declared relationship and pick up the declared known information (e.g. 'The first is the media bill', 'Three causes are visible in the numbers', 'Answering Ingrid's question needs precise words', 'Recording provenance is not bookkeeping', 'Those failing PDFs were documents', 'The sanitize stage exists because', 'Hearthly's bill comes next', 'Derivatives can be regenerated; masters cannot', 'The Barcelona review turned on a hash match', 'Hashing compares photos with each other; image models read each photo', 'Julien's two documents describe one failure', 'Stripping GPS coordinates from photos closes one way'). One boundary fails, below.

results.draft_locus: Perceptual Hashing: Finding the Same Photo Twice ¶5
results.quote: The Lyon apartment shows the other side:
results.finding: Declared contrast carrying over 'a shared index that catches copied photos'. The opening says 'the other side' without naming what it is the other side of; the preceding paragraph ends on brands' trust rules, so the contrast (a cross-seller match that is legitimate, not fraud) is left for the reader to reconstruct, and 'The Lyon apartment' is used as if already introduced. Both flow readers stopped here.

Both readers describe the declared order (problem scene, terms, pipeline with privacy, the bill's half, the ring's half, image uses beyond fraud and rich media, evidence and plan, judgement sections), say the roadmap announces it and the body keeps to it, and mark no section UNCLEAR. Points judged not material: 'Common Ground' (A3.7, B3.7) is on audience.already_knows; Keybridge in the trade-offs table (A3.8, B3.6) is glossed in the same cell as 'a neutral SaaS' and the March 2027 decision is explained in the next paragraph; the CDN-purge pointer (A3.3) is a spec-required forward pointer the reader itself called small.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: 1.8 Billion Images and a Fake-Rental Ring ¶1
results.quote: A third finding, from Tradeyard, is already on her list: the stored originals of Femke's bike photos still carry the GPS coordinates of her home.
results.finding: Both readers stopped: a 'third' finding arrives before the first and second documents are described, and Femke is named with no clause saying who she is (a private seller on Tradeyard). The spec only requires the finding to be on Ingrid's list in this paragraph; the prose can say who Femke is and present it as a separate finding without numbering it ahead of the documents.

results.quote: Those failing PDFs were documents, not photos, and the document path needs rules of its own, because in jobs and real estate it carries personal data.
results.finding: Both readers found the paragraph announcing 'rules of its own' that it never gives here (A: they arrive only in the retention table two sections later; B: stranded, repeats stage 4). The spec's controlling idea (documents are media assets with personal data and their own retention) can be kept in place by naming the rules or pointing to the malware-scan stage and the Documents retention class.

The spec order (sharing, then the legitimate-match case) is workable if the opening names the contrast explicitly.

Terms on does_not_know are given before or where first used: media asset, original, master (glossed in the introduction as 'cleaned uploads'), derivative, image service, content addressing, perceptual hash, PDQ and Hamming distance in Concepts; EXIF GPS tags in Privacy; AVIF/WebP as modern formats with browser support; storage-class minimum durations and retention classes in Storage Tiers; the publication budget and trust decision in the timing split with their owning chapters. Common Ground, Keybridge, Tradeyard and the cast are on already_knows. One unintroduced referent fails, below.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: 1.8 Billion Images and a Fake-Rental Ring ¶1
results.quote: the stored originals of Femke's bike photos still carry the GPS coordinates of her home
results.finding: Femke is not on already_knows (she is a private seller, not book cast) and the scene names her without saying who she is; she is identified only in the Privacy section. Both flow readers reported her as unintroduced.

The introduction opens with a concrete intriguing comparison (kilobytes of text vs megabytes of photos times derivatives and years), bridges from the attribute dictionary and the reader's staged media stack, states the thesis and gives a roadmap; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', adds no new subtopic or body evidence, and does not end on a rephrased thesis alone: it synthesizes the two documents into one failure and one contract, then hands off to location-and-geo by similarity.

It states what no single section states (the bill and the ring are one failure, answered by one contract whose entry step removes copies and fills the hash index while on-demand derivatives and lifecycle remove renditions and undeleted masters) and says why it matters: sharing the contract and index first is cheap, cuts the bill and stops fraud earlier without waiting for storage to move.

It returns to the scene's callback element: 'Julien's two documents describe one failure', and answers Ingrid's question in substance (stores less, catches stolen photos earlier; privacy in the GPS hand-off).

The cold reader lists all sixteen expected sections in the spec's roadmap order (scene with bill and ring, terms, pipeline and publication checks, what photos reveal, derivatives and CDN, storage tiers and lifecycle, perceptual hashing, image understanding beyond fraud, video/tours/floor plans, public examples, Hearthly's plan in numbers, trade-offs, vertical differences, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, review questions), the evidence (fictional Veldmark, public examples, cost numbers) and a plain declarative tone.

Reader names all expected elements: the match only made a 'possible duplicate' queue item while the listing went live; it returned a distance with no seller relationship; the index covered one brand. Fix: for high-risk segments such as rentals, feed the match to the trust decision before searchable and hold the listing, attach the seller relationship, share the index across brands, use block lists.

Reader names the three causes (feed re-downloads without change markers, nine stored renditions kept forever, no deletion of ended-listing media) and the fixes (SHA-256 masters with conditional requests, hash comparison and media change dates; on-demand derivatives behind a CDN in AVIF/WebP with bounded widths; lifecycle by listing state with colder classes and deletion by retention class). It omits the parenthetical about minimum storage durations, which the chapter covers in the lifecycle section; the causes and changes the probe asks for are all given.

Reader answers no: stored originals keep GPS and one misconfigured bucket exposes the home; strip metadata in sanitization before the master is written, keep raw originals only for a documented purpose with restricted access and short retention, and purge derivatives from the CDN on deletion. Matches the expected answer.
